blindSummary:
The national prosecution service's 2012-2021 study records 10 of the country's 88 LGTB homicides (Jan 2012-May 2021) in this state/province - the national capital's districts account for 12, adjacent capital-area districts for 10, 7, 6 and 6 - centred on this state/province's largest city. The region's population share (~3%) is far smaller than its homicide share (~11.4%), giving a per-capita lethality roughly 3.8 times the rate recorded elsewhere in the country: a materially concerning concentration not explained by population alone.

Counterweight: a 2024 regional labour-inclusion ordinance (regional council session 3 September 2024, approved 6 September 2024, published in the official gazette November 2024) promotes labour inclusion of trans and gender-nonconforming people - their right to formal, dignified work in equitable conditions without discrimination on gender identity or expression, and recognition of the trans community as a vulnerable group. This is a resident-facing instrument (a visitor does not use it), but it evidences that this particular regional council legislated visibly for trans inclusion - the one such ordinance found across this country's 26 first-level units. It also sits in the same unit where community self-governance bodies exercise recognised dispute-resolution authority, a structural caveat with no documented trans-specific case. The multi-year dataset here is more robust evidence than single-incident records elsewhere.
blindSourceSummaries: The national prosecution service's press note (23 Mar 2022) for its study of intentional killings of LGTB people, Jan 2012-May 2021: 84 criminal complaints covering 88 victims and 72 accused; 58% of deaths in six areas (national capital 12, this state/province 10, adjacent capital-area districts 10, 7, 6, 6); victims mostly gay men (55.8%) and trans women (36.4%), adults 25-54 (72.7%), 94.3% of national nationality; perpetrators mostly men (94.4%), known or family (26.4%) or partners/ex-partners (26.4%); 47.7% occurred in victims' own homes; case-file motive recorded common crime (21.6%) with no motive data in 45.5%, but press-review analysis estimates 68.9% show bias-violence indicators. Study by the prosecution service's observatory with the national justice ministry and a university public-health observatory, UNDP support.

The regional government of this state/province: a 2024 regional labour-inclusion ordinance - approved at regional council session 3 September 2024 (6 September 2024) - promotes labour inclusion of trans and gender-nonconforming people in this state/province; guarantees the right to formal, dignified, productive work in equitable conditions without discrimination on gender identity or its expression, and recognises the trans community as a group in a situation of vulnerability.

Official gazette text of the same 2024 regional labour-inclusion ordinance, issued in this state/province's largest city, 6 September 2024: promotes labour inclusion of trans and gender-nonconforming people; grounded in the national constitution (equality and non-discrimination articles) and the regional-government framework (decentralisation statutes); issued under the region's ordinance-making competence.
blindOutOfScope: Community self-governance bodies (dispute-resolution authority in parts of this state/province) are structural context relevant to general order, not trans-specific: no documented trans case involving it. General crime and political instability affect all travellers; the assessment reflects trans-specific risk only.
